body:
Thanks for reporting.

https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/27407 takes care of the issue

Thanks @geoand for the fix!

If I understand the test in your PR correctly, then it will work with @JvmStatic in the future, right? Is it also possible to avoid that we even need the @JvmStatic? I know it is just a small convenience thing, so no worries if it would be a lot of effort. But if it is possible, I think it would be great to support the more Kotlin idiomatic way as well :)

> f I understand the test in your PR correctly, then it will work with @JvmStatic in the future, right?

Correct

>  Is it also possible to avoid that we even need the @JvmStatic

I am not sure how this could be done TBH, but it might be possible

So what I understand from the Kotlin docs (https://kotlinlang.org/docs/java-to-kotlin-interop.html#static-methods), a "normal" Kotlin Companion object method (without @JvmStatic) could be called by calling

`SwapiRestClient .Companion.toException()`

So it should be possible to check if there is a static object named "Companion" on the rest client class and check if that has one of the annotated methods.
That is correct. It's a little less than ideal to require `@JvmStatic` on kotlin code that won't necessarily be Java code facing but this is certainly better than nothing.
